extracted.intended_audience: government trade authorities, anti-dumping investigators, trade lawyers, and policymakers implementing or assessing anti-dumping measures under GATT
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for determining dumping, assessing material injury or threat, conducting investigations, and imposing/collecting anti-dumping duties under Article VI/GATT and the Anti-dumping Code. Covers definitions, evidentiary rules, provisional measures, undertakings, and duration/review of duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of dumping
rubrics_metrics.description: A product is to be considered as being introduced into the commerce of another country at less than its normal value if the export price is less than the comparable price in the exporting country for the like product when destined for consumption in the exporting country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article VI (1)(a) and Anti-dumping Code Article 2(a). Also recognizes alternative tests in Article VI(1)(b) (highest comparable export price to a third country or cost of production plus reasonable addition for selling cost and profit). 'Due allowance' shall be made for differences in conditions and terms of sale, taxation, and other differences affecting price comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Like product definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'like product' shall be interpreted to mean a product which is identical, i.e. alike in all respects to the product under consideration, or, in the absence of such a product, another product which ... has characteristics closely resembling those of the product under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-dumping Code Article 2(b). Use identity or close resemblance to determine the comparator for price and injury analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison when imports via intermediate country
rubrics_metrics.description: When products are exported to the country of importation from an intermediate country, the price at which products are sold from the country of export to the country of importation shall normally be compared with the comparable price in the country of export.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-dumping Code Article 2(c). Exception: comparison may be made with the price in the country of origin if products are merely trans-shipped, not produced in country of export, or no comparable price exists in country of export.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of margin of dumping when no domestic sales
rubrics_metrics.description: When there are no sales of the like product in the ordinary course of trade in the domestic market of the exporting country ... the margin of dumping shall be determined by comparison with a comparable price of the like product when exported to any third country (representative price) or with the cost of production in the country of origin plus reasonable amounts for administrative, selling and other costs and for profits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-dumping Code Article 2(d). As a general rule, addition for profit shall not exceed the profit normally realized on sales of products of the same general category in the domestic market of the country of origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructed export price where export price unreliable
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no export price or the export price appears unreliable because of association or compensatory arrangements, the export price may be constructed on the basis of the price at which the imported products are first resold to an independent buyer, or on such reasonable basis as authorities may determine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-dumping Code Article 2(e). Used where related-party transactions or other factors make declared export prices unreliable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair comparison requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To effect a fair comparison, export price and domestic price shall be compared at the same level of trade, normally at the ex-factory level, and in respect of sales made as nearly as possible the same time; due allowance shall be made for differences in conditions and terms of sale, taxation, and other differences affecting price comparability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-dumping Code Article 2(f). In cases of constructed prices, allowance for costs incurred between importation and resale and for profits accruing should be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal-cause standard for material injury
rubrics_metrics.description: A determination of injury shall be made only when the authorities are satisfied that the dumped imports are demonstrably the principal cause of material injury or threat of material injury to a domestic industry or the principal cause of material retardation of establishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-dumping Code Article 3(a). Determination must be based on positive findings and not on mere allegations or hypothetical possibilities; when assessing retardation of a new industry, convincing evidence of forthcoming establishment must be shown (e.g., factory construction, machinery ordered).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to be examined in injury evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The evaluation of injury shall be based on examination of all factors having a bearing on the state of the industry such as: development and prospects with regard to turnover, market share, profits, prices (including delivered duty-paid price compared to comparable price), export performance, employment, volume of dumped and other imports, utilization of capacity, productivity and restrictive trade practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-dumping Code Article 3(b)-(c)-(d). No single factor necessarily decisive; authorities must also examine other factors adversely affecting the industry (e.g., undumped imports, internal competition, contraction in demand, substitution). Where domestic production lacks separate identity, examine the narrowest group for which information is available; assess effects relative to domestic production criteria like production process and producers' realizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threat of material injury standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A determination of threat of material injury shall be based on facts and not merely on allegation, conjecture or remote possibility; the change in circumstances which would cause material injury must be clearly foreseen and imminent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-dumping Code Article 3(e)-(f). Cases of threatened injury require special care in application of anti-dumping measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'domestic industry'
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'domestic industry' shall be interpreted as referring to the domestic producers as a whole of the like products or to those whose collective output constitutes a major proportion of total domestic production of those products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-dumping Code Article 4(a). Exceptions: (i) where producers are importers, the industry may refer to the rest of producers; (ii) in exceptional circumstances a country may divide production into two or more competitive markets and treat producers within each as a separate industry (only if injury affects all or almost all production in that market). Article 4(b) treats integrated multi-country markets as a single industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation and termination of investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations shall normally be initiated upon a request on behalf of the industry affected, supported by evidence of dumping and injury. An application shall be rejected and an investigation terminated promptly as soon as authorities are satisfied there is not sufficient evidence of either dumping or injury. Immediate termination where margin, volume, or injury is negligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-dumping Code Article 5(a)-(c). Authorities may in special circumstances initiate investigations on their own if they have evidence of both dumping and injury. Anti-dumping proceedings shall not hinder customs clearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence, participation, confidentiality and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign suppliers and all other interested parties shall be given ample opportunity to present in writing and, on justification, orally, all evidence; complainant, importers, exporters and exporting governments shall be allowed to see all non-confidential information used by authorities; confidential information shall be treated as strictly confidential unless the authorities find confidentiality unwarranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-dumping Code Article 6(a)-(d),(f)-(h),(i). Authorities may investigate in other countries with firms' agreement (6(e)). Parties must be notified when competent authorities are satisfied that sufficient evidence exists to justify initiating an investigation (6(f)). Authorities shall provide opportunity for defense, meetings between opposing parties, and must notify representatives of exporting country and directly interested parties of decisions with reasons and criteria and, unless special reasons, make decisions public (6(g)-(h)). If interested party withholds necessary information, final finding may be made on facts available (6(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Price undertakings (voluntary price revision or cessation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-dumping proceedings may be terminated without imposition of duties or provisional measures upon receipt of a voluntary undertaking by exporters to revise prices so that the margin of dumping is eliminated or to cease exporting at dumped prices, if authorities consider this practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-dumping Code Article 7(a)-(b). If undertaking accepted, investigation of injury may still be completed at exporters' or authorities' request. If a no-injury determination is made, the undertaking automatically lapses unless exporters state otherwise. Failure to offer an undertaking shall not prejudice consideration of the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision and limits on imposition/amount of anti-dumping duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision whether or not to impose an anti-dumping duty and whether the amount shall be the full margin or less are decisions to be made by authorities of the importing country. It is desirable that imposition be permissive and that duty be less than the margin if adequate to remove injury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-dumping Code Article 8(a). The amount of duty must not exceed the margin of dumping as established (8(c)). If duty collected exceeds actual margin, excess shall be reimbursed promptly (8(c)). Duties should be levied on a non-discriminatory basis on imports from all sources found to be dumped and causing injury, and authorities shall name supplier(s) or supplying country(ies) (8(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic-price system rules for duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Within a basic price system, if several suppliers are involved anti-dumping duties may be imposed equivalent to the amount by which the export price is less than the basic price established for this purpose, not exceeding the lowest normal price in the supplying country where normal competition prevails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-dumping Code Article 8(d). For products sold below established basic price a new investigation shall be carried out when demanded by interested parties with relevant evidence. Reimbursement rules apply if duties collected exceed actual dumping margin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation of duties to defined market area
rubrics_metrics.description: When the industry has been interpreted as producers in a certain area (market), anti-dumping duties shall only be definitively collected on products consigned for final consumption to that area, except where exporter is given opportunity to cease dumping in that area and adequate assurance is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-dumping Code Article 8(e). If assurances are not given or fulfilled, duties may be imposed without limitation to an area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of anti-dumping duties and review
rubrics_metrics.description: An anti-dumping duty shall remain in force only as long as it is necessary to counteract dumping which is causing injury. Authorities shall review the need for continued imposition on their own initiative or if interested suppliers or importers request review and submit substantiating information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-dumping Code Article 9(a)-(b). Periodic review and responsiveness to requests for review are required where warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional measures conditions and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional measures may be taken only when a preliminary decision has been taken that there is dumping and when there is sufficient evidence of injury. They may take the form of a provisional duty or a security (deposit or bond) equal to the provisionally estimated duty, not greater than the provisionally estimated margin of dumping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-dumping Code Article 10(a)-(b),(c),(d),(e). Authorities must inform exporting country representatives and interested parties of decisions and criteria (10(c)). Provisional measures shall be limited to as short a period as possible — not longer than three months or, upon agreement of exporter and importer, six months (10(d)). Relevant provisions of Article 8 apply to provisional measures (10(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Retroactivity rule (limited)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-dumping duties and provisional measures shall only be applied to products which enter for consumption after the time when the decision ... enters into force, except that in cases: ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-dumping Code Article 11 (opening provision). (Full exceptions not included in this excerpt.) Authorities generally may not apply duties retroactively to shipments entered before decision enters into force, subject to specified exceptions.
